name: Cataclysm
caption: GWF's own championship-collecting faction, built around Chris O'Malley, SheltonSplash and James Murphy, absorbing Don Cicinni after Rise and Fall III.
notes: Roster and arc per Chris O'Malley's own held bio card (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-chris-omalley.html): formed by SheltonSplash and James Murphy around O'Malley, later took in Don Cicinni; broke down with Cicinni's departure, SheltonSplash's injury and James Murphy's betrayal. Fielded as a team (with Bryan Daniels and XO Malone allied to it) in the 27 April 2008 War Games (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html).

name: Numbered Toast
caption: The Number 4 and Michael Toaster's own tag pairing, GWF Tag Team Champions as of the 27 April 2008 War Games, before the two split acrimoniously.
notes: Held the GWF Tag Team Championship during the 27 April 2008 War Games (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html), where the pair walked out and padlocked their own opponents inside the cage rather than lose the titles cleanly. By 2013's 20113 the belts had changed hands (to Neo-Evolution) off the surviving record.

name: Neo-Evolution
caption: Kevin McAuliffe and GWF owner Dave Shadow's own tag pairing, GWF Tag Team Champions by 2013, lost at the closing show.
notes: Named per Chris O'Malley's own bio card (Kevin McAuliffe and Dave Shadow feuding with Cataclysm's tag champions in 2007-08). Fought together in the 27 April 2008 War Games on the winning side. Lost the GWF Tag Team Championship to Danny Mainer and Bryan Daniels at 20113 (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html), 20 January 2013 — a separate SND-card-era document names Chris Williams as Kevin McAuliffe's own "former Neo-Evolution partner" instead of Dave Shadow (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-snd-card-2009-04-04.html); the surviving record does not resolve this discrepancy, recorded honestly rather than silently reconciled.

name: The Movement
caption: XO Malone's own faction, fielding Damian DeNiro alongside a masked "Sinister Minister" as ringside muscle; won the GWF Tag Team Championship from SheltonSplash and Kevin McAuliffe in an undated match recapped only in flashback.
notes: The tag-title win is recounted only as a flashback clip inside SheltonSplash's own 5 April 2009 promo, "The Living Fairytale" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/rp-the-living-fairytale.html) — no date recoverable. "The Movement" also interferes, under that name, in the 27 June 2008 Mini FNB main event (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/mini-fnb.html), where its ringside pair is XO and "Sinister Minster" (sic) rather than Damian DeNiro — the surviving record shows the group's own membership shifting rather than fixed, recorded as attested rather than reconciled.

name: The Ministry of Darkbread
caption: Mark Madison's own first GWF stable, recruited around his early "Underbaker" gimmick — remembered for going nowhere, save for the notorious promo the fed's own Hall of Shame credits to member Biscotti 2 Hotty.
notes: Per the fed's own Hall of Shame induction thread (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/hos-induction-7-28-08.html): managed by a Paul Cooker (unminted — a manager named only in this one retrospective post); Todd Caroon won a battle royal to keep his job in his only match, then never wrestled again.

name: The Food Division
caption: A June–July 2006 wave of food-parody gimmicks chasing Toast Hogan's Cruiserweight Championship, never itself including Toast Hogan and banished by SheltonSplash that August.
notes: Per the fed's own Hall of Shame induction thread (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/hos-induction-7-28-08.html), the loosely-affiliated origin point of both Chris O'Malley (as "The Roll") and Mark Madison (as "The Underbaker").

name: The GWF Spirit Squad
caption: A five-man male cheerleading squad and GWF's own earliest stable, a WWE-clone gimmick from the fed's first weeks in 2006 that folded after one member walked and the rest lost to DX.
notes: Per the fed's own Hall of Shame induction thread (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/hos-induction-7-28-08.html): active from the 3rd episode of Friday Night Brawl (5 May 2006); beat GWF jobber Shadowprince and GWF legend John Beanshaw Wrathfield (by countout) before Wolfenstein's own "Spirit Breaker" loss to Tadg30 ended the group, the rest then losing to DX (unminted — a one-line mention, no roster or staged match recovered). Wolfenstein alone went on to a GWF Championship reign; Lodis3 to three Hardcore Championship reigns (unminted — named only in this same retrospective).
